english.heading: Food Forest Design
body: Build a living food system in layers.
Grow food from tall canopy down to root crops.
Use vertical space, soil life, shade, and moisture together.
Learn how to design and establish a food forest for your farm.

heading.text: Pulane ya Ḓaka ḽa Zwiḽiwa
heading.backTranslation: Pulane ya Ḓaka ḽa Zwiḽiwa [Plan of the Food Garden/Food Forest [?]]

body.text: Fhaṱani sisiteme ya zwiḽiwa i tshilaho nga miṱaṱo.
body.backTranslation: Build a food system that lives by layers.

body.text: Alusani zwiḽiwa u bva kha canopy ya miri milapfu u swika kha zwimela zwa midzi (root crops).
body.backTranslation: Grow food from the canopy of tall trees down to root crops (root crops).

body.text: Shumisani tshikhala tsha nṱha na fhasi, vhutshilo ha mavu, muthunzi na maḓi a kha mavu zwo ṱangana.
body.backTranslation: Use the space above and below, soil life, shade and the water in the soil together.

body.text: Gudani u pulana na u thoma ḓaka ḽa zwiḽiwa kha bulasi ḽaṋu.
body.backTranslation: Learn to plan and to start a food garden on your farm.

english.heading: Why This Matters
body: A food forest grows useful plants at different heights.
Good design can combine harvests, shade and soil cover. Plants still compete for light, water and nutrients.
Plan the care you can provide and watch how the planting changes.

heading.text: Ndi ngani hezwi zwi zwa ndeme

body.text: Ḓaka ḽa zwiḽiwa ḽi alusa zwimela zwi shumiseaho kha vhulapfu ho fhambanaho.
body.backTranslation: A food forest grows plants that are used at different heights.

body.text: Pulane yavhuḓi i nga ṱanganya khaṋo, muthunzi na u fukedza mavu. Zwimela zwi kha ḓi ṱaṱisana nga tshedza, maḓi na nutrients dza mavu.
body.backTranslation: A good plan can combine shade, canopy and covering the soil. Plants still compete for light, water and soil nutrients.

body.text: Pulani ṱhogomelo ine na nga i ita, ni dzule ni tshi sedza uri zwimela zwi khou shanduka hani.
body.backTranslation: Plan the care that you can do, and keep watching how the plants are changing.

english.heading: Learning Outcomes
body: Name the seven commonly described food-forest layers.
Check plants against your site, local ecology and the approved project list.
Plan establishment and ongoing care without assuming a fixed date for harvest or canopy closure.

heading.text: Zwine na ḓo kona u zwi ita
heading.backTranslation: What you will be able to do

body.text: Ṋeani madzina a miṱaṱo 7 ya ḓaka ḽa zwiḽiwa ine ya anzela u ṱalutshedzwa.
body.backTranslation: Give the names of 7 layers of a food forest that are often explained.

body.text: Sedzani uri zwimela zwi tshi fana na fhethu haṋu, ecology ya fhethu na approved project list.
body.backTranslation: Look that the plants are like your place, the ecology of the place and the approved project list.

body.text: Pulani ṱhogomelo ya tshifhinga tsha u dzhia midzi na ṱhogomelo i tshi bvela phanḓa, ni sa humbuli uri hu na ḓuvha ḽo tiwaho ḽa khaṋo kana ḽa u valwa ha canopy.
body.backTranslation: Plan the care for the time of taking roots and for the care to continue, not assuming that there is a fixed day of harvest or of closing of the canopy.

english.heading: The Forest Uses Every Layer
body: An indigenous forest fills the space from the highest branches to the roots.
Different plants use the light and moisture available at their level.
A food forest copies this pattern with productive species.
The result is not one crop in one row, but many useful layers growing together.

heading.text: Ḓaka ḽi shumisa miṱaṱo yoṱhe

body.text: Ḓaka ḽa indigenous ḽi ḓadza fhethu u bva kha maṱavhi a nṱhesa u swika kha midzi.
body.backTranslation: An indigenous garden fills the place from the high branches down to the roots.

body.text: Zwimela zwo fhambanaho zwi shumisa tshedza na maḓi zwi re hone kha muṱaṱo wazwo.
body.backTranslation: Different plants use the light and water that are there in their shade/canopy [?].

body.text: Ḓaka ḽa zwiḽiwa ḽi edzisa nḓila heyi nga zwimela zwi bveledzaho.
body.backTranslation: The food garden imitates this way with plants that produce.

body.text: Mvelelo a si tshiliṅwa tshithihi kha muduba muthihi, fhedzi ndi miṱaṱo minzhi i shumiseaho i tshi aluwa i tshi ṱangana.
body.backTranslation: The result is not one crop on one bed, but many used layers [?: miṱaṱo = plantings/trees/layers] growing while they meet together.

english.heading: Watch: Read the Seven Planting Layers
body: Find seven planting layers.
Tall trees form the canopy.
Smaller trees grow below it.
Then look for woody shrubs.
Herbaceous plants have soft stems.
Ground cover spreads across the surface.
Root crops grow below the surface.
Climbers use suitable supports.
These are planning layers, not fixed height bands. Choose plants and spacing for your site.

heading.text: Sedzani: Vhalani Miṱaṱo 7 ya U Ṱavha

body.text: Wanani miṱaṱo 7 ya u ṱavha.
body.backTranslation: Find the 7 cuts/prunings.

body.text: Miri milapfu i vhumba canopy.
body.backTranslation: Tall trees form the canopy.

body.text: Miri miṱuku i aluwa nga fhasi hayo.
body.backTranslation: Small trees grow beneath it.

body.text: Zwa u tevhela, ṱoḓani zwiṱaka zwi re na thanda dza muri dzo khwaṱhaho.
body.backTranslation: Next, look for shrubs that have strong tree branches [?].

body.text: Zwimela zwa herbaceous zwi na thanda dzi si dza muri, dzi sa khwaṱhaho.
body.backTranslation: Herbaceous plants have branches that are not woody and not strong.

body.text: Zwimela zwi fukaho fhasi zwi a ṱandavhuwa nṱha ha mavu.
body.backTranslation: Plants that creep on the ground spread above the soil.

body.text: Zwimela zwa midzi (root crops) zwi aluwa fhasi ha mavu.
body.backTranslation: Root crops (root crops) grow under the soil.

body.text: Zwimela zwi gonyaho zwi shumisa zwithu zwi tikedzaho zwi fanelaho zwa u gonya khazwo.
body.backTranslation: Climbing plants use suitable supports to climb on.

body.text: Heyi ndi miṱaṱo ya u pulana, a si mitshetshelo yo tiwaho ya vhulapfu. Nangani zwimela na tshikhala zwi tshi ya nga fhethu haṋu.
body.backTranslation: These are layers for planning, not set measurements of height. Choose plants and space according to your place.

english.heading: The Seven Layers
body: Think of tall canopy, smaller trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants.
Ground cover protects the surface, root crops grow below it, and climbers use suitable supports.
The heights and spacing depend on the plants and site. These are planning layers, not fixed height bands.

heading.text: Miṱaṱo 7

body.text: Humbulani nga ha canopy ya miri milapfu, miri miṱuku, zwiṱaka na zwimela zwa herbaceous.
body.backTranslation: Think about the canopy of tall trees, small trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants.

body.text: Zwimela zwi fukaho fhasi zwi tsireledza mavu a nṱha, zwimela zwa midzi zwi aluwa fhasi hayo, nahone zwimela zwi gonyaho zwi shumisa zwithu zwi tikedzaho zwi fanelaho.
body.backTranslation: Ground-covering plants protect the topsoil, root crops grow beneath it, and climbing plants use suitable supports to climb on.

body.text: Vhulapfu na tshikhala zwi ya nga zwimela na fhethu. Heyi ndi miṱaṱo ya u pulana, a si mitshetshelo yo tiwaho ya vhulapfu.
body.backTranslation: Height and space depend on the plants and the place. These are layers for planning, not set measurements of height.

english.heading: Read a Layered Planting Example
body: The original Highveld example includes Wild Fig or pecan above lemon, naartjie and black mulberry.
It places Cape gooseberry and Wild Medlar with vegetables, wild garlic, sweet potato and granadilla.
Treat this as a layout example, not permission to plant every species. Check identity, frost tolerance, mature size and local restrictions first.

heading.text: Vhalani Tsumbo ya U Ṱavha nga Miṱaṱo
heading.backTranslation: Count the Example/Guide of the Pruning by Cuts

body.text: Tsumbo ya mathomo ya Highveld i katela Wild Fig kana pecan nṱha ha lemon, naartjie na black mulberry.
body.backTranslation: The starting example of the Highveld includes Wild Fig or pecan above lemon, naartjie and black mulberry.

body.text: Tsumbo heyo i vhea Cape gooseberry na Wild Medlar na miroho, wild garlic, sweet potato na granadilla.
body.backTranslation: That example places Cape gooseberry and Wild Medlar with vegetables, wild garlic, sweet potato and granadilla.

body.text: Dzhiani heyi sa tsumbo ya u dzudzanya, hu si tendelo ya u ṱavha species dzoṱhe. Phanḓa ha u ṱavha, khwaṱhisedzani uri zwimela ndi mini, frost tolerance, vhukhulu ha zwimela zwo aluwa zwo fhelela na thivhelo dza fhethu.
body.backTranslation: Take this as an example of arrangement, not as permission to plant all species. Before planting, confirm what the plants are, frost tolerance, the size of the fully grown plants and local restrictions.

english.heading: Care Changes as Plants Grow
body: Young plants need establishment care: moisture checks, weed control and protection from damage.
As plants grow, shade and leaf litter change conditions below them.
Check competition and access. Prune, thin or adjust lower planting when observations call for it; the system does not become care-free on a fixed birthday.

heading.text: Ṱhogomelo i a shanduka zwimela zwi tshi aluwa

body.text: Zwimela zwiṱuku zwi ṱoḓa ṱhogomelo ya establishment: u sedza maḓi a kha mavu, u langa zwimela zwi sa ṱoḓeaho na u zwi tsireledza kha u sinyea.
body.backTranslation: Small plants need establishment care: watching the water in the soil, controlling unwanted plants and protecting them from damage.

body.text: Musi zwimela zwi tshi aluwa, muthunzi na leaf litter zwi shandukisa nyimele fhasi hazwo.
body.backTranslation: When plants grow, shade and leaf litter change the conditions beneath them.

body.text: Sedzani ṱaṱisano na nḓila ya u swikelela. Gunyulani maṱavhi, ni ite thinning (u bvisa zwimela zwo nangiwaho) kana ni lugise zwimela zwa fhasi musi ni tshi vhona uri zwi a ṱoḓea; sisiteme a i vhi ya u sa ṱoḓa ṱhogomelo nga ḓuvha ḽo tiwaho ḽa u bebwa.
body.backTranslation: Watch competition and access. Prune, do thinning (removing selected plants), or adjust the lower plants when you see it is needed; the system does not become care-free on a set birthday.

english.heading: Choose for Your Site
body: Check local rainfall, frost, heat, soil and water availability before choosing plants.
Mango can suffer frost damage. Quince needs suitable winter chilling for reliable cropping.
A regional label or a sheltered corner is not enough. Confirm each plant and variety with reliable local guidance.

heading.text: Nangani Zwi Fanelaho Fhethu haṋu

body.text: Sedzani mvula ya fhethu, mutsho wa frost, vhudifhi, mavu na u vha hone ha maḓi phanḓa ha u nanga zwimela.
body.backTranslation: Look at local rainfall, frost cold, heat, soil and the availability of water before choosing plants.

body.text: Mango i nga vhaisala nga mutsho wa frost. Quince i ṱoḓa winter chilling i fanelaho uri i bveledze mitshelo nga nḓila i fulufhedzeaho.
body.backTranslation: Mango can be hurt by frost cold. Quince needs suitable winter chilling so that it can produce fruit reliably.

body.text: Dzina ḽa vhupo kana kona ḽo tsireledzwaho a zwi ngo linga. Khwaṱhisedzani tshimela tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe na cultivar yatsho nga nyeletshedzo i fulufhedzeaho ya fhethu.
body.backTranslation: The name of the region or a protected corner is not enough. Make sure each plant and its cultivar with reliable local information.

english.heading: Watch: Match the Species to the Climate
body: Climate decides which species belong.
On the Highveld, choose cold-tolerant trees and shrubs; on the KZN coast and Lowveld, choose warm-climate species.
Match every plant to your site.

heading.text: Sedzani: Fhelekedzani Zwimela na Climate

body.text: Climate i nanga uri ndi zwimela zwifhio zwi fanelaho.
body.backTranslation: Climate chooses which plants are suitable.

body.text: Kha Highveld, nanganini miri na zwiṱaka zwi kondelaho mutsho; kha KZN coast na Lowveld, nanganini zwimela zwa fhethu ha u fhisa.
body.backTranslation: On the Highveld, choose trees and shrubs that withstand frost; on the KZN coast and the Lowveld, choose plants of hot places.

body.text: Fhelekedzani tshimela tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe na fhethu haṋu.
body.backTranslation: Match each plant to your place.

english.heading: Check the Highveld Examples
body: The original list includes pecan, walnut and indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry and loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry and Barbados cherry.
This list is not a blanket recommendation. Check each plant against frost, soil, mature size and the approved local species list.
Keep existing legal and project restrictions in force. Do not plant from a picture alone.

heading.text: Sedzani Tsumbo dza Highveld

body.text: Ḽisiti ya mathomo i katela pecan, walnut na indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry na loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry na Barbados cherry.
body.backTranslation: The first list includes pecan, walnut and indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry and loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry and Barbados cherry.

body.text: Heyi ḽisiti a si tsivhudzo ya zwimela zwoṱhe kha fhethu hoṱhe. Sedzani tshimela tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe nga mutsho wa frost, mavu, vhukhulu ha zwimela zwo aluwa zwo fhelela na approved local species list.
body.backTranslation: This list is not a recommendation of plants for everywhere in all places. Check each plant by frost cold, soil, size of fully grown plants and the approved local species list.

body.text: Dzulisani thivhelo dza mulayo na dza project dzo no vha hone dzi tshi kha ḓi shuma. Ni songo ṱavha nga u sedza tshifanyiso fhedzi.
body.backTranslation: Respect the legal restrictions and project restrictions that already exist and are still in force. Do not plant just by looking at the illustration.

english.heading: Check the Warm-Region Examples
body: The original warm-region examples include mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry and Wild Dagga.
Marula, Mopane and baobab also appear in the Limpopo examples. Local suitability still needs checking.
Useful trees are not automatically edible. Confirm identity and safe use; a landscape photograph is not a food-identification guide.

heading.text: Sedzani Tsumbo dza Fhethu ha u Fhisa
heading.backTranslation: Look at Examples of a Hot Place

body.text: Tsumbo dza mathomo dza fhethu ha vhudifhi dzi katela mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry na Wild Dagga.
body.backTranslation: First examples for the hot area include mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry and Wild Dagga.

body.text: Marula, Mopane na baobab zwi a vhonala na kha tsumbo dza Limpopo. U fanela ha fhethu hu kha ḓi ṱoḓa u sedzwa.
body.backTranslation: Marula, Mopane and baobab are also seen in the Limpopo examples. Suitability of the place still needs to be checked.

body.text: Miri i shumiseaho a zwi ambi uri i nga liwa. Khwaṱhisedzani uri ndi mini na u i shumisa nga tsireledzo; tshifanyiso tsha vhupo a si nḓila ya u ḓivha zwiḽiwa.
body.backTranslation: A tree that is used does not say that it can be eaten. Confirm what it is and use it safely; a picture of a place is not a way to know food.

english.heading: Include Locally Appropriate Indigenous Plants
body: Locally appropriate indigenous plants can support habitat as part of the design.
Choose for your ecosystem and the useful role of each plant. There is no sourced percentage target in this lesson.
Protect existing natural vegetation. Do not turn healthy grassland into a food forest simply because trees are useful elsewhere.

heading.text: Katelani zwimela zwa indigenous zwi tea fhethu
heading.backTranslation: Include indigenous plants that are suitable for the place

body.text: Zwimela zwa indigenous zwi fanelaho fhethu zwi nga tikedza habitat sa tshipiḓa tsha pulane.
body.backTranslation: Indigenous plants suited to the place can support habitat as part of the plan.

body.text: Nangani zwi tshi ya nga ecosystem yaṋu na mushumo une wa thusa wa muṅwe na muṅwe wa zwimela. Kha ino ngudo a hu na tshipikwa tsha phesenthe tshi sumbedzwaho uri tshi bva ngafhi.
body.backTranslation: Choose according to your ecosystem and the helpful function of each plant. In this study there is no percentage target indicated as to where it comes from.

body.text: Tsireledzani zwimela zwa mupo zwo no vha hone. Ni songo shandukisa fhethu ha mahatsi hu re na mutakalo u vha ḓaka ḽa zwiḽiwa fhedzi nga ngauri miri i na mushumo kha fhethu huṅwe.
body.backTranslation: Protect natural plants that already exist. Do not change a healthy grassland into a food forest only because the trees have a function in some places.

english.heading: Plan the Sequence for the Site
body: Start by checking the site, water supply and care available. Protect exposed soil early.
Temporary support plants may provide shelter and useful cut material where appropriate.
Main trees and lower layers can be introduced as conditions allow. Ground cover need not wait until the end; avoid plants competing with young trees.

heading.text: Pulani Tevhekanyo ya Mishumo Fhethu haṋu
heading.backTranslation: Plan the Order of Jobs in Your Place

body.text: Thomani nga u sedza fhethu, maḓi a re hone na ṱhogomelo i re hone. Tsireledzani mavu o vuleaho nga u ṱavhanya.
body.backTranslation: Begin by looking at the place, the water that is there and the care that is there. Protect exposed soil quickly.

body.text: Support plants dza tshifhinganyana dzi nga ṋea tsireledzo na zwipiḓa zwo gunyulwaho zwi shumiseaho hune ha fanela.
body.backTranslation: Temporary support plants can give protection, and pruned parts can be used where suitable.

body.text: Miri ya ndeme na miṱaṱo ya fhasi zwi nga ḓisiwa musi nyimele dzi tshi tendela. Zwimela zwi fukaho fhasi a zwi ṱoḓi u lindela u swika magumoni; dzivhani zwimela zwi tshi ṱaṱisana na miri ine ya kha ḓi aluwa.
body.backTranslation: Important trees and lower layers can be brought in when conditions allow. Ground-covering plants do not need to wait until the end; avoid plants competing with trees that are still growing.

english.heading: Watch: Care for a Young Food Forest
body: This picture shows a young food forest. Start with an area you can care for.
Protect exposed soil early. Here, loose mulch covers the soil.
Keep mulch away from the trunk. Notice the clear space at the tree's base.
Watch for competition. The farmer is removing grass near the young tree.
Before adding more plants, check moisture, shelter and the care you can provide. Let what you observe guide your next step.

heading.text: Sedzani: Ṱhogomelo ya Ḓaka ḽa Zwiḽiwa ḽi Aluwaho
heading.backTranslation: Look: Care of a Growing Food Forest

body.text: Tshifanyiso itshi tshi sumbedza ḓaka ḽa zwiḽiwa ḽi kha ḓi aluwa. Thomani nga fhethu hune na nga kona u hu ṱhogomela.
body.backTranslation: This picture shows a food forest [?] that is still growing. Start at a place where you are able to care for it.

body.text: Tsireledzani mavu o vuleaho nga u ṱavhanya. Henefho, mulch yo sa vhofhelelwaho i fhukedza mavu.
body.backTranslation: Protect open soil quickly. There, mulch that is not tied/blocked [?] covers the soil.

body.text: Vhulungani mulch kule na tsinde ḽa muri (trunk). Vhonani tshikhala tshi si na tshithu fhasi ha muri.
body.backTranslation: Keep mulch away from the tree trunk. Look at the empty space beneath the tree.

body.text: Sedzani ṱaṱisano. Mulimi u khou bvisa mahatsi a re tsini na muri u kha ḓi aluwa.
body.backTranslation: Watch competition. The farmer is removing grass near a tree that is still growing.

body.text: Phanḓa ha u engedza zwimela zwiṅwe, sedzani maḓi a kha mavu, tsireledzo na ṱhogomelo ine na nga i ita. Zwine na zwi vhona zwi ni livhise kha vhukando vhu tevhelaho.
body.backTranslation: Before adding other plants, look at the water in the soil, protection and the care that you can do. What you see leads you to the next step.

english.heading: Prepare a Manageable First Area
body: Begin with an area you can water and maintain. Check existing vegetation before clearing.
Where appropriate, plain cardboard under suitable mulch can suppress unwanted growth. Keep water able to enter the soil and leave trunks clear.
Plan spacing from mature plant size. Prepare nursery plants for the next suitable planting opportunity.

heading.text: Lugisani Fhethu ha u Thoma hu nga Ṱhogomelwaho
heading.backTranslation: Prepare a Starting Place that Can Be Cared For

body.text: Thomani nga fhethu hune na nga hu nwesa maḓi na u hu ṱhogomela. Sedzani zwimela zwo no vha hone phanḓa ha u bvisa.
body.backTranslation: Start at a place that you can water and take care of. Look at the plants that are already there before removing.

body.text: Hune ha fanela, cardboard i si na zwo ṅwaliwaho kana zwifanyiso fhasi ha mulch i fanelaho i nga fhungudza zwimela zwi sa ṱoḓeaho. Dzulisani maḓi a tshi nga dzhena kha mavu, ni siye matsinde a miri (trunks) a si na tshithu tshi a kwamaho.
body.backTranslation: Where suitable, cardboard with no writing or pictures beneath suitable mulch can reduce unwanted plants. Let water be able to enter the soil, and leave the tree trunks with nothing touching them.

body.text: Pulani tshikhala nga vhukhulu ha zwimela zwo aluwa zwo fhelela. Lugisani nursery plants u itela tshifhinga tshi tevhelaho tshi fanelaho tsha u ṱavha.
body.backTranslation: Plan space according to the size of the fully grown plants. Prepare nursery plants for the next suitable time of planting.

english.heading: Adjust as the Trees Grow
body: Watch how shade, roots and available water affect neighbouring plants.
Comfrey and wild garlic appear in the original underplanting example; check their local suitability before use.
Prune or thin support plants when needed, using methods suited to each species. Suitable clean cuttings can return as mulch. Do not wait for a fixed year if competition is already harming plants.

heading.text: Shandukani Musi Miri i tshi Aluwa

body.text: Sedzani uri muthunzi, midzi na maḓi a re hone zwi ita hani kha zwimela zwa tsini.
body.backTranslation: Check how shade, roots and the water available affect nearby plants.

body.text: Comfrey na wild garlic zwi a vhonala kha tsumbo ya mathomo ya u ṱavha fhasi ha miri; sedzani u fanela hazwo fhethu haṋu phanḓa ha u zwi shumisa.
body.backTranslation: Comfrey and wild garlic appear in the first planting example under trees; check their suitability at your place before using them.

body.text: Gunyulani maṱavhi kana ni ite thinning ya support plants musi hu tshi ṱoḓea, ni tshi shumisa nḓila dzi fanelaho species iṅwe na iṅwe. Zwipiḓa zwi tshena zwo gunyulwaho zwi fanelaho zwi nga dovha zwa shumiswa sa mulch. Ni songo lindela ṅwaha wo tiwaho arali ṱaṱisano yo no thoma u vhaisa zwimela.
body.backTranslation: Prune or thin support plants when needed, using methods suited to each species. Suitable clean pruned parts can be reused as mulch. Do not wait for a fixed year if competition has begun to hurt the plants.

english.heading: Plant with Reliable Moisture
body: Choose a planting opportunity when soil moisture and expected weather support establishment.
Rain can help, but check the root zone and keep a backup watering plan. Avoid planting into waterlogged ground.
Check young plants after planting. Harvest timing and outside inputs depend on the species, site and care; there is no guaranteed fifth-year result.

heading.text: Ṱavhani ni na Maḓi a Mavu a Fulufhedzeaho
heading.backTranslation: Prune/plant while having reliable soil water

body.text: Nangani tshifhinga tsha u ṱavha musi maḓi a kha mavu na nyimele ya tshifhinga ine ya lavhelelwa zwi tshi tikedza establishment.
body.backTranslation: Choose the planting time when there is water in the soil and the expected weather conditions support establishment.

body.text: Mvula i nga thusa, fhedzi sedzani root zone ni vhe na pulane ya u nwesa maḓi i shumiswaho arali mvula i sa wa. Dzivhani u ṱavha kha mavu o ḓalaho maḓi.
body.backTranslation: Rain can help, but check the root zone and have a plan for the watering to be used if the rain does not fall. Avoid planting in soil that is full of water.

body.text: Sedzani zwimela zwiṱuku musi zwo no ṱavhiwa. Tshifhinga tsha khaṋo na zwi ḓisiwaho u bva nnḓa zwi ya nga species, fhethu na ṱhogomelo; a hu na mvelelo i khwaṱhisedzwaho ya ṅwaha wa vhuṱanu.
body.backTranslation: Check the small plants once they have been planted. The time of growth and of what is brought in from outside depends on species, place and care; there is no guaranteed result for the fifth year.

english.heading: Field Assignment
body: Draw the layers for your own proposed planting. Mark access, water and existing natural vegetation.
Record local frost, rain, soil and available care.
For each plant from the approved list, record its intended role and the local advice still needed before planting.

heading.text: Mushumo wa tsimuni

body.text: Olani miṱaṱo ya u ṱavha haṋu ho pulaniwaho. Sumbedzani nḓila ya u swika, maḓi na zwimela zwa mupo zwo no vha hone.
body.backTranslation: Draw your planned cuts/pruning places. Show the access path, the water and the natural plants that are already there.

body.text: Ṅwalani mutsho wa frost, mvula, mavu na ṱhogomelo ine ya wanala fhethu haṋu.
body.backTranslation: Write the frost cold, rain, soil and care that are found in your place.

body.text: Kha tshimela tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe kha approved list, ṅwalani mushumo une na ṱoḓa uri tshi u ite na nyeletshedzo ya fhethu i kha ḓi ṱoḓea phanḓa ha u ṱavha.
body.backTranslation: For each plant on the approved list, write the job you want it to do and the information about the place that is still needed before pruning/planting.

english.heading: Field Action
body: Inspect a manageable area and choose one next step.
Protect exposed soil, check plant suitability, or prepare nursery plants.
Plant only when conditions and follow-up care are suitable. Return to the same spot to check survival, soil moisture and competition.

heading.text: Nyito ya tsimuni

body.text: Ṱolisisani fhethu hune na nga kona u hu ṱhogomela, ni nange vhukando vhuthihi vhu tevhelaho.
body.backTranslation: Examine closely the place that you can take care of, and choose one next step.

body.text: Tsireledzani mavu o vuleaho, sedzani arali zwimela zwi tshi fanelea fhethu, kana ni lugise nursery plants.
body.backTranslation: Protect exposed soil, check whether plants suit the place, or prepare nursery plants.

body.text: Ṱavhani fhedzi musi nyimele na ṱhogomelo i tevhelaho zwi tshi fanela. Vhuyani fhethu huthihi u sedza u tshila, maḓi a kha mavu na ṱaṱisano.
body.backTranslation: Prune only when the condition and the following care are suitable. Return to the same place to check survival, water in the soil and competition.
